reviews.body: Claiming the event in the same transaction is the right call.

comments.author: dan
comments.body: This is a POST that changes money state. Shouldn't it have @idempotent like the other ones (ADR-004)?

comments.author: alice
comments.body: Good question, and why I left the comment above it. @idempotent keys on the Idempotency-Key header, which Stripe doesn't send. Stripe retries with the same event id, so we dedupe on that in `processed_events.claim`, in the same transaction as the state change. Inbound provider webhooks are the exception; our own client-facing POSTs still need the decorator.

threads.rejection_reason: Provider webhooks dedupe on the provider event id instead of @idempotent.
